subject: literature
passage: Nusrat had grown up in Dhaka, and she spent the long bus ride to her cousins' village listing everything she would miss: fast internet, her favorite café, the hum of the city at night. On her first evening, the power went out during a heavy monsoon rain. Her cousin Rafiq lit a lantern, and the family gathered on the veranda to tell stories while rain drummed on the tin roof. Nusrat, who had planned to go to bed early, was still listening when the lantern burned low near midnight. The details suggest that Nusrat ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: was frightened by the storm and afraid to go to her room alone.
choices.B: had decided to move to her cousins' village permanently.
choices.C: found the evening more enjoyable than she had expected to.
choices.D: still wished she had stayed in Dhaka instead of visiting.

explanation.why: Nusrat expected to miss city life and planned to go to bed early, yet she stayed up until midnight listening to the family's stories. Her change of plans shows that the evening turned out better than she had imagined.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests fear; she stayed to listen to the stories, not to avoid being alone.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Enjoying one evening does not show that she planned to live in the village for good.
explanation.C: Correct. She meant to go to bed early but stayed up until midnight, showing she enjoyed the evening.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Staying up late with the family suggests she was not longing to be back in the city that night.
